title: Evals quality scratchpad — summarization/regression notes
content:
Goal: quick scratchpad for recent summarization regressions and ad-hoc rubrics. Notes to self + sample outputs and immediate follow-ups.

Context:
- Running comparison between model-v2.2 (baseline) and model-v2.3 (recent infra+quant changes).
- Dataset: 800 doc->summary pairs from internal summarization benchmark (mix of long news, product docs, and meeting transcripts).
- Observed: overall ROUGE1 slightly up (~+0.6), but human QA indicates higher hallucination rate on numeric facts and dropped fidelity on long contexts.

Ad-hoc rubric (for quick manual labels) — 1..5 scale, notes for labelers:
- Fidelity: Does the summary accurately reflect facts in source? (5 = fully accurate, 1 = major factual errors)
- Hallucination: Does the summary introduce unsupported facts? (5 = none, 1 = multiple fabrications)
- Coherence/Fluency: Readability and grammaticality (5 = trivial edits, 1 = incomprehensible)
- Conciseness/Redundancy: Is it concise and not repetitive? (5 = tight, 1 = rambling)
- Usefulness: Would a product user rely on this summary? (5 = yes, 1 = no)

Quick mapping: for aggregate scoring compute average of Fidelity & Hallucination & Usefulness (weight fidelity x0.5, hallucination x0.3, usefulness x0.2) — rough, just for triage.

Sample cases (short excerpts):
1) Long meeting transcript (context length ~12k tokens)
- Source snippet: "We agreed to shift Q3 roadmap to focus on latency, deprioritized feature X, budget hold until legal review closes (expected July 14)."
- model-v2.2 summary: "Team will shift Q3 roadmap to focus on latency, put feature X on hold, and pause budget until legal review completes in mid-July." (Fidelity 5, Hallucination 5, Coherence 5)
- model-v2.3 summary: "We will change the Q3 roadmap to improve latency, cancel feature X, and freeze budget until legal says OK in August." (Fidelity 3, Hallucination 2, Coherence 5)
- Notes: v2.3 introduced an incorrect commitment ("cancel" vs "deprioritize") and pushed the date to August (hallucinated). Looks like compression/beam changes cause date artifacts.

2) Product doc with numeric specs
- Source snippet: "Throughput target: 5k rps per instance with p99 <50ms on NVIDIA A100, expected cost $0.12/token"
- v2.2 summary: "Throughput target 5k rps, p99 <50ms on A100; cost target $0.12/token." (Fidelity 5, Hallucination 5)
- v2.3 summary: "Throughput 5k rps, p99 <20ms on A100; cost $0.08/token." (Fidelity 2, Hallucination 1)
- Notes: clear numeric hallucination on latency and cost. Reproducible across multiple seeds. Suspect quantized kernels cause rounding errors in numeric extraction module.

Regression observations (patterns):
- Numeric hallucinations: v2.3 tends to shorten numbers (e.g., 50ms -> 20ms) or change currency/token cost. High confidence in the model output despite being wrong.
- Commitment verbs shift: stronger verbs introduced ("cancel" vs "deprioritize"). Potentially due to tighter prompt compression and changed decoding temperature.
- Long-context fidelity drop around 8k+ tokens: summaries omit earlier decisions and hallucinate later dates. Possibly KV-cache truncation heuristics changed.
- Overall surface metrics (ROUGE/BLEU) are noisy: small improvements mask quality regressions important to customers.

Immediate checks to run (priority ordered):
- [ ] Run focused eval on 1k numeric-containing examples across models v2.2/v2.3 to quantify numeric hallucination rate. (link JIRA-1198)
- [ ] Re-run a subset with decoding temperature fixed to v2.2 value to see if verb strengthening is decoding-related.
- [ ] Inspect KV-cache logs for long contexts to see if cache hits drop off near 8k token boundary. Ask infra to enable extra tracing for a few requests. (cc @Noah Kim)
- [ ] Add explicit numeric-probe prompts to eval harness (e.g., "What is the p99 latency mentioned in the doc?") and capture answer confidence/entropy.
- [ ] Create 50 gold-labeled samples for "commitment verb" edge cases to measure verb strength shift.

Labeler notes / calibration:
- Emphasize exactness for numeric fields — if a number is different by >5% mark as fidelity issue.
- If the model invents a date/month/year not present in source, mark as hallucination regardless of plausibility.
- For long transcripts, if the summary misses a "decision" (e.g., budget hold) mark fidelity down by 2 points.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Did any infra change in v2.3 touch the tokenizer or byte-pair merges? That could shift numeric parsing. (TODO: check release-engineering PRs)
- Is there a correlation between sequence length and hallucination confidence? Need scatterplot of token-length vs confidence/hallucination flag.
- Are certain prompt templates more robust? Quick A/B with few-shot exemplars vs instruction-only could help.

Quick experiment plan (this week):
- 2026-03-30: run numeric-only eval (1k samples) and verb-strength mini-set (50 samples).
- 2026-03-31: analyze results, slice by doc type (news, product, transcript).
- 2026-04-01: draft short findings note and recommended rollback or prompt fixes.

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc minimal — canonical writeup will go into CON-7842 once I have solid numbers.
- Sam to check decoding parameters in the serving config (Sam, assign me the run id).
- Noah to add KV-cache debug for 5 failing traces.

Last quick heuristics I tried (local):
- For 20 failing cases, adding a prefix template "Extract exact numeric values from the following doc:" reduced numeric hallucination by ~30% for v2.3. Promising but might add verbosity cost.
- Lowering temperature from 0.9 to 0.6 reduced verb-strength errors but also reduced recall on optional details. Tradeoff.

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Attach failing examples to JIRA-1198 (will add after numeric eval completes)
- [ ] Add 50 gold-labeled verb-strength examples to eval repo (issue created)
- [ ] Consider prompt-level guardrails for numeric extraction in product pipelines

-- end scratchpad --
